title: Room temperature chemical upcycling of poly(bisphenol A carbonate)  via  solvent- and catalyst-free aminolysis
content: This study reports a green and sustainable method for the chemical recycling of polycarbonate (PC) plastic waste and the concurrent production of valuable 2-imidazolidinones via amine-induced depolymerization under solvent- and catalyst-free conditions at room temperature. Under these mild conditions, PC polymer is rapidly cleaved to produce bisphenol A (BPA) with 94% yield and a high-value 2-imidazolidinone (IMD) with 80% yield, through a practical isolation protocol. This method was applied to post-consumer PC plastics, such as safety goggles, bike helmet shields, and mobile phone cases, achieving good yields of BPA and IMD products. The structural characterization of BPA and IMD was confirmed by single-crystal XRD, NMR, and FT-IR techniques. In a co-valorization approach integrating plastic and biomass feedstocks, the reaction of shredded compact disc PC waste with biomass-derived furfurylamine was successfully scaled to a 15 g batch, affording BPA in 84% yield along with a 66% yield of the biomass-based urea derivative (1,3-bis(furan-2-ylmethyl)urea). Green chemistry metrics and technoeconomic analysis underscore the environmental and economic advantages of the developed recycling technology for the PC plastic industry. Overall, the study establishes a practical, room temperature, solvent- and catalyst-free platform for upcycling PC plastic waste into value-added building blocks, contributing to more sustainable management of PC plastics.
